headline: AP calls first House seat to change hands, in North Carolina's 11th district; Republicans win Senate races in Florida, West Virginia and Wyoming
body: The Associated Press has called North Carolina's 11th congressional district for Democrat Jamie Ager, according to the Guardian's live results tracker, which carries AP race calls. The seat is currently held by Republicans, making it the first House seat of the night to change party. With about 88% of the expected vote counted, the tracker shows Ager on 59.0% and Republican Jennifer Balkcom on 39.6%. In the Senate, AP has called five more races: Republican holds in Florida (Ashley Moody), West Virginia (Shelley Moore Capito) and Wyoming (Harriet Hageman), and Democratic holds in Colorado (John Hickenlooper) and New Mexico (Ben Ray Luján). That brings Senate calls to 14: 11 for Democrats and 3 for Republicans, with North Carolina the only seat to change hands so far. In the House, the tracker shows 103 races called: 71 for Democrats and 32 for Republicans, with 218 needed for a majority. AP race calls are media calls, not official results; counting continues and neither chamber has been called.

headline: AP calls North Carolina Senate race for Roy Cooper, the first seat to change hands tonight
body: The Associated Press has called North Carolina's Senate race for Democrat Roy Cooper, according to the Guardian's live results tracker, which carries AP race calls. The seat is currently held by Republicans, making it the first Senate seat of the night to change party. With about 60% of the expected vote counted, the tracker shows Cooper on 65.3% and Republican Michael Whatley on 33.0%. AP has also called New Hampshire's Senate race for Democrat Chris Pappas, a Democratic hold, with about 23% of the expected vote counted. That brings Senate calls to nine, all for Democrats. In the House, the tracker shows 54 races called: 37 for Democrats and 17 for Republicans, with 218 needed for a majority. AP race calls are media calls, not official results; counting continues and neither chamber has been called.

headline: AP calls Senate races in Georgia, New Jersey, Illinois and three more states for Democrats
body: The Associated Press has called six more Senate races as Democratic holds, according to the Guardian's live results tracker, which carries AP race calls. AP called Georgia, one of the night's closely watched seats, for Jon Ossoff, and also called the races in New Jersey (Cory Booker), Illinois (Juliana Stratton), Massachusetts (Ed Markey), Delaware (Chris Coons) and Rhode Island (Jack Reed). With Virginia called earlier, that makes seven Senate calls, all Democratic holds, with no seat changing hands so far. In the House, the tracker shows 38 races called: 25 for Democrats and 13 for Republicans, with 218 needed for a majority. AP race calls are media calls, not official results; counting continues and much of the vote in many states is still to be reported. Neither chamber has been called.

headline: First race calls: Democrats hold Virginia's Senate seat; early House calls in Kentucky and Florida
body: With the first polls closed across the East, the first race calls of the night have come in. The Guardian's live results tracker, which shows Associated Press race calls, has Democrats holding the Senate seat in Virginia. In the House, it shows Democrats holding Kentucky's 3rd district and Florida's 10th, and Republicans holding Kentucky's 5th. These are media projections, not official results; state counts continue and certification comes weeks later. Neither chamber has been called. AP says control of the Senate could take days to settle and the House up to about a week, with ranked-choice tabulation possible in Alaska and Maine. Democrats need to flip four Senate seats and three House seats to win control, according to AP.
